additional_info.subject: 0437487 - ID0437487-DC/Si-D/TR-[Y2/T4 314241502042] Charger doesn't turn on CRM:00314000192
additional_info.body:
Good morning Furkan,
I am reaching out regarding ticket
ID0437487.
I am summarizing here the findings from today's onsite support:
The charger could not turn on, and it was discovered from your side that TB17 was not producing any 24 Vdc.
After you replaced the TB17, the charger was able to turn on and go online on SCB. However, we noticed the following errors:
The charger seems unable to close the mainbreaker QA1.
You mentioned that the customer complained that, when the charger is powered on with QA2 (which affects only L3 and N), there is an unbalance in the income Ac phases. Therefore, we measured the phases with QA2 closed, and we noticed:
L1-N 245 Vac
L2-N 222 Vac
L3-N 202 Vac
N-PE 25 Vac
There is a clear unbalance of the phases, and we can also see voltage between the Neutral conductor and PE.
With QA2 open, the Phase Voltages are balanced, and
between N-PE we measure 2 Vac
.
I believe we have a case of fluctuating neutral,
i.e neutral conductor not correctly/perfectly connected to PE from grid side. In the past, we had a similar case where it was found that in the grid cabinet there was a loose connection between PE-N.
Furthermore:
Sicharge D can only be supplied by line supply types TN-C, TN-S and TT (as stated in "Operating Instructions SICHARGE D" manual under "Technical specifications" chapter).
In the charger, if any loads (components) have a dispersion or an abnormal absorption, we would see a variation only of the voltage value of L3, if N was properly connected to ground. We would not see L3 decreasing and L1 and L2 increasing their voltage value, creating an unbalance.
This behavior is possible only if the N conductor coming from the grid is not correctly connected to the PE conductor from grid side, or if it is an IT supply line, which is not compatible with Sicharge D installation requirements.
Therefore, it is necessary to perform an inspection of the power supply coming from the grid with the DSO, for:
Verification of the connection between N conductor and PE conductor.
Verification of phase shift between L1, L2 and L3.
Verification of integrity of phase fuses coming from the grid, to avoid compensation of a missing phase.
Please get in contact with the grid provider and verify the points above. I will be waiting for your feedback and results after this inspection.
With kind regards,

Dear Furkan,
I am writing to formally inform that we are moving case 0437487 ﻿from the
Technical Support
to the
eMobility RC-TR SI E Queue (Level 2)
, due to one or more following reason (s):
During several onsite activities, it was observed that the issue comes from the grid, specifically a floating neutral. Depending on the load applied to the L3 phase from the charger side, this results in an imbalance in grid voltages, with differences of up to 25V measured between the N (neutral) and PE (protective earth) conductors.
We recommend contacting your grid provider to inspect the connection between N and PE on the grid side, ensuring it complies with the specifications of the permitted grid system.
As there are no further actions required from our side, we are handing over the ticket to your queue.
